transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-09
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Carter (Redwood AE), Anita Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood Solutions Eng); Liam O'Connor (AuroraPay Head of Platform), Maya Chen (ML Eng), Rafael Gomez (Security), Sophia Park (PM)

[00:00] Jamie Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros 1 i'm jamie from redwood, with anita and marcus on the engineering side. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Good, thanks. we'll kick off quick: main goal here is to scope the poc for the customer service chat + reconciliation summarization use cases. want to make sure we size capacity right and get realistic latency/cost numbers.
[00:28] Anita Desai: great. to do that we need a bit of workload characterization 1 qps, concurrency, typical input/output token counts, and success criteria. maybe maya can give the current traffic shape?
[00:40] Maya Chen: sure. quick caveat 1 i'm speaking from memory, i'll send exact traces later. for chat assist we're seeing average ~12 qps across the east/us region, but spikes to 140-160 qps during promo peaks. concurrency for the model layer today sits around 45-60 active sessions during peaks. most requests are short 1 median input ~35-50 tokens, 90th perc about 110-120. outputs vary: quick replies ~30-80 tokens, but our reconciliation summaries are longer, avg ~180 tokens, 95th ~350.
[01:18] Marcus Li: ok that variance matters 1 short chat vs long summarization. for batching and kv cache behavior, the longer outputs will increase per-request GPU time. what's your goal p95 latency?
[01:30] Sophia Park: for chat we want p95 < 400ms ideally, but we can accept up to 800ms for the longer reconciliation jobs as long as throughput is predictable. cost is also a big factor 1 we have a cost target of less than $X per 1M tokens but we'll be more concrete after your model suggestions.
[01:48] Anita Desai: understood. for the poc we usually run two profiles: a latency SLO profile (representative small prompts, target p95) and a throughput/cost profile (longer outputs and sustained qps). we'll need sample prompts and a traffic histogram.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: we'll provide an anonymized week of traffic traces and the top 100 prompt templates. question on deployment: we'd prefer dedicated capacity if latency spikes are common, but we're open to hosted for faster time-to-value. security will weigh in.
[02:22] Rafael Gomez: yes 1 from security we need encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration, audit logs, and VPC peering or PrivateLink. also interested in model isolation and data retention for the poc.
[02:36] Jamie Carter: totally 1 we have a private deployment option and Dedicated pools that integrate with customer KMS and VPC. we'll include our security pack. for sizing, can you confirm the ratio of chat vs reconciliation traffic?
[02:47] Maya Chen: right now about 80% chat, 20% recon by request count, but recon accounts for ~45% of token volume due to longer outputs.
[02:58] Marcus Li: good to know. so initial modeling: if average qps is 12 and peak 160, with 60 concurrency, a single Dedicated pool with autoscale can handle that but we need to choose instance types and model quantization. are you planning to use an open model or commercial?
[03:15] Liam O'Connor: open models for cost reasons, but we'd like redwood to advise on the best candidate. we've tested a few Llama-family variants and some quantized checkpoints.
[03:26] Anita Desai: we'll propose 2 model variants: an optimized smaller model for chat (lower latency) and a larger one for summaries, with smart routing and fallback. for the poc we'll run both and measure quality tradeoffs.
[03:38] Maya Chen: curious 1 how do you handle kv cache across short chat sessions vs long sessions? we worry about cache misses during bursts.
[03:48] Marcus Li: our runtime manages kv cache per session and can spill or evict based on policy. for the poc we'll instrument cache hit rates. that will be part of the benchmark metrics we collect.
[03:58] Liam O'Connor: timeline question 1 what's a realistic poc timeline? we're aiming to decide by end of month.
[04:05] Jamie Carter: typical poc is 2-3 weeks: week 0 setup and security review, week 1 synthetic benchmarks and initial runs, week 2 real-traffic replay and tuning, optional week 3 extended tests. if you want a dedicated sizing run we can do that in week 1.
[04:20] Sophia Park: sounds good. can you map benchmarks to success criteria? we need clear pass/fail to move to Dedicated purchase.
[04:27] Anita Desai: yes. typical success criteria for this customer would be: 1) latency: p95 chat < 400ms on hosted or <300ms on Dedicated; 2) throughput: support peak bursts up to 160 qps within 2x autoscale window; 3) cost: projected token cost within your internal target (we'll model); 4) quality: summaries >= 0.88 f1 on your eval set or no regression vs current baseline. we can adjust thresholds with you.
[04:54] Maya Chen: quality metric 1 we have a small eval harness for recon tasks; we'll share it. are you able to run A/B style evals during the poc?
[05:02] Anita Desai: yes, we can do rollouts and A/B tests and capture quality metrics. we'll also capture token-level cost and breakdowns per request.
[05:12] Rafael Gomez: for security gating, we need SOC2 type II evidence, encryption, and network design. we will not send PII in traces; we'll redact before sharing.
[05:21] Jamie Carter: perfect. we'll send SOC2/ISO docs and a redwood security summary.
[05:26] Marcus Li: back to traffic modeling 1 maya, can you give a rough distribution for input token lengths? you mentioned medians; any percentiles?
[05:33] Maya Chen: median input 40 tokens, 75th 80, 90th 120, 99th 420 (rare). outputs: median 60, 75th 140, 90th 300, 99th 800 for some long recon dumps.
[05:47] Marcus Li: okay that tail will affect batching. for modeling we'll create two synthetic workloads: workload A (chat-heavy, short outputs) and workload B (recon-heavy, long outputs). we'll run each at avg and peak qps and measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost.
[06:01] Liam O'Connor: for peak testing do you recommend replaying production traces or synthetic ramp?
[06:06] Anita Desai: both 1 replay gives fidelity for prompt distribution and payload sizes; synthetic ramp helps explore worst-case sustained qps. we'll need your traces to do replay correctly.
[06:15] Sophia Park: what about concurrency limits per session? we have some long-lived sessions open that generate multiple calls 1 that might increase concurrency beyond request qps estimates.
[06:25] Marcus Li: that's a common pattern; we'll ask you to mark session ids in the trace so we can compute concurrent open sessions. it informs cache retention and memory sizing.
[06:35] Maya Chen: we can add session ids. next 1 instrumentation: what metrics will you give us during the poc?
[06:41] Anita Desai: we'll provide token-level cost, per-route p50/p95/p99 latencies, batch sizes, cache hit rates, GPU utilization, and error rates. also per-request traces for failed cases.
[06:51] Rafael Gomez: please include audit log samples and where logs are stored for compliance.
[06:56] Jamie Carter: will do. ok let's talk numbers for Dedicated sizing: if you want consistent p95 <300ms for chat and handle 160 qps peaks, we recommend starting with 4x A100x2 or equivalent with autoscale to add 2 nodes at 60% utilization1we'll finalize after running a synthetic benchmark against your traces.
[07:18] Liam O'Connor: that seems reasonable. cost estimate ballpark?
[07:22] Jamie Carter: very rough 1 depends on model and quantization. small optimized model on Dedicated could cut token cost by ~40% vs unoptimized larger model. we'll provide a cost model spreadsheet in the benchmark template.
[07:34] Sophia Park: okay. on the model side, do you offer quantized checkpoints and can we test mixed-precision?
[07:40] Anita Desai: yes 1 we support 8-bit and 4-bit quantization and will surface expected accuracy regressions. for the poc we'll run a quantized variant and a baseline float-16 variant to compare.
[07:52] Maya Chen: any limits on request size or streaming behavior? we sometimes stream partial results to UI.
[07:58] Marcus Li: streaming supported for incremental responses. large requests will still consume tokens proportionally; streaming doesn't change compute but helps perceived latency in UI.
[08:08] Liam O'Connor: good. can you outline the benchmark plan live?
[08:12] Anita Desai: sure 1 plan overview: Phase 0 (setup & security) 2-3 days; Phase 1 (synthetic benchmark): run workload A and B at average qps for baseline; Phase 2 (stress/peaks): ramp to peak qps and sustained runs to test autoscale; Phase 3 (replay real traces): replay your week of traces and collect metrics; Phase 4 (quality eval): run A/B on your eval set. deliverables: benchmark report, recommended Dedicated config, cost projection, and runbook for rollout.
[08:48] Sophia Park: turn-around times?
[08:51] Jamie Carter: once we get traces and access, we can do Phase 1 in 3 business days and deliver initial numbers; full replay + quality eval ~7-10 business days. so overall 2-3 weeks.
[09:05] Maya Chen: sounds aligned. about authentication 1 we need SSO and RBAC for access to logs and dashboards.
[09:12] Rafael Gomez: and we might require IP allowlists and VPC peering 1 will these be supported in the poc?
[09:18] Jamie Carter: yes, for Dedicated and Private deployments we support VPC peering, PrivateLink and allowlisting. for hosted we have admin console RBAC and audit logs but we can do Private control plane for stricter network controls.
[09:30] Liam O'Connor: ok let's capture concrete acceptance criteria.
[09:34] Anita Desai: i'll propose this set: 1) p95 chat < 400ms on hosted or <300ms on Dedicated for representative small prompts, 2) system supports bursts up to 160 qps without >2x latency degradation, 3) projected token cost for expected monthly volume within your target, 4) quality regression <5% vs your baseline on recon eval, 5) security review passed (docs provided). these are negotiable.
[10:00] Sophia Park: good. one more ask 1 we want per-route cost metrics so we can make product tradeoffs.
[10:06] Marcus Li: we'll include per-route token breakdowns and cost allocation in the report.
[10:11] Maya Chen: how will you simulate user think-time and session behavior in replay?
[10:15] Anita Desai: when you provide traces we'll include timestamps and session ids and replay with original inter-arrival times. for synthetic tests we'll create ramp profiles with adjustable think-times.
[10:27] Liam O'Connor: okay 1 next practical step is we share redacted traces and prompts. is there anything else you need from our side?
[10:33] Jamie Carter: traces, eval harness, token cost target if you have one, and security contacts. we'll send the benchmark template and security pack after this call.
[10:40] Rafael Gomez: i'll coordinate security info 1 expectation is we review SOC2 and network diagrams before handing any data.
[10:46] Sophia Park: timeline for pricing and proposal?
[10:48] Jamie Carter: we'll include a POC pricing estimate in the same email as the benchmark template, and a dedicated capacity proposal after the sizing run. expect initial numbers within 48 hours.
[10:58] Anita Desai: small note 1 when replaying, please include any special tokens or system messages you inject; they can change token counts significantly.
[11:06] Maya Chen: will do.
[11:09] Liam O'Connor: thanks everyone 1 last question: can we run a quick sample test during the poc setup to validate networking?
[11:15] Marcus Li: yes, a networking smoke test can be done in phase 0. we'll coordinate with rafael.
[11:22] Jamie Carter: great. i'm going to recap next steps now.
[11:26] [Recap] Jamie Carter: Action items 1 jamie to send benchmark template & security pack by 2026-04-11/12; anita to draft recommended Dedicated config by 2026-04-14; maya to share redacted traces and eval harness by 2026-04-13; rafael to share security requirements by 2026-04-11. We'll schedule a 1-hour sizing run early next week.
[11:50] Sophia Park: thanks 1 sounds good.
[11:54] Liam O'Connor: appreciate it.
[12:00] Jamie Carter: thanks, everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
[12:06] [END OF CALL]

Notes on metrics to collect during POC:
- QPS (avg / peak) per route
- Concurrency and concurrent session counts
- Input/output token histograms (p50/p75/p90/p99)
- Per-request p50/p95/p99 latencies
- Batch sizes and batch latency impact
- KV cache hit rate and cache memory usage
- GPU utilization and time-per-token
- Error rates and fallback counts
- Token-level cost and per-route cost allocation

References mentioned: benchmark template (will be sent), security pack (SOC2/ISO), cost model spreadsheet.
